counterexample_without_persistence.laws: member 0 reads its draw, member 1 always B, member 2 reads its draw; tau = 1 everywhere

stopping_time_form_p_2/3.note: tau(w) is the first position whose member gives one guess for both draws at the history w reaches; the stopping-time form, a candidate core lemma, needs persistence as a premise (every member from tau(w) on ignores its draw at the history w reaches), which BHW meets since its cascades are absorbing; checked here on BHW only (the Lean fixes k)

D_stochastic_bound.statement_checked: If every member from k on has |P(A | a, h) - P(A | b, h)| <= eps_n at every history reachable at its position, the act list's law moves by at most the sum of eps_n in total variation between any two assignments of the later draws (a hybrid argument; not proved in Lean; a candidate periphery lemma, since the core has no probability).

hybrid: own draw w.p. 1/2, else counting
leaky 1/2 (reads the next member's draw; own D = 0)
rows.note: outside Turns: the member-wise premise holds and the bound does not apply

D_stochastic_bound.note_on_the_sum_form: total variation is at most 1, so the sum-of-eps check can fail only in rows whose sum is below 1: here only the two BHW rows without flips (sum 0); every other row meets it trivially
D_stochastic_bound.weighted_statement: For assignments a, b of the later draws, TV <= sum over the positions j where they differ of E|D(k + j, h)|, h drawn from the law of the history at k + j under the draws of one assignment before j (the hybrid argument; the smaller of the two orders is used). Not in the Lean; it can lie below 1. For every member in Turns it holds by the hybrid argument and data processing, so its check verifies the simulator, not the members. It is attained at pairs differing in one draw and is loose at the pairs of largest total variation where members read (the hybrids and the logit rows).
